reasons.why: The profile is 100% conversation by items and by chars (ChatMessage, Chat and ChatThread nodes). The rule for a single-type graph is to take the strategy of the dominant data type, so conversation is the match. On the tune split it ties the default at 0.9 (n 60, se 0.0391), so there is no measured gain and I claim none. The strategy's build keys are recorded but not applied in this run. They fit the message lengths (p50 442, p90 2548 chars). No entities step: no model cost is justified, and the profile shows email in 40 items and phone in 78 items, which are sensitive. No custom strategy is needed because the built-in conversation covers the data type.

No query-key override. Every candidate scores 0.9, identical to the default, with se 0.0391 on n 60. A difference of 0 is under two standard errors, so it is noise. The tune figures support no change, so the default bm25_name, bm25_path and bm25_body stay.
